findings.title: Avoid interpolating expanded targets again during execution
findings.body: These expanded targets are still passed to `datasource.runQuery()`, whose backend-query preparation applies template variables again. Sharded queries also arrive here already expanded by `runShardSplitQuery()`. Template replacement is not idempotent: if a single-valued variable `label` contains the literal value `$region`, `{label="$label"}` first becomes `{label="$region"}` and the next pass replaces that literal with the dashboard's `region` value. Enabling splitting can therefore change label or filter values and return incorrect results. The execution path needs to avoid re-interpolating targets expanded here; the new tests mock `runQuery()` and do not exercise that path.

findings.title: Filter empty expressions after interpolation
findings.body: The previous implementation filtered empty expressions after interpolation, but this implementation filters only the original expressions. A target whose entire expression is a variable resolving to an empty string now remains in `splittingTargets`. When such a target is placed in the non-sharded group alongside a valid sharded query, that group reaches `runSplitQuery()`, which removes its blank target and constructs no requests. `runSplitGroupedQueries()` then dereferences `[0].partition` on the empty request list and throws, preventing the valid queries from completing. Retain the post-interpolation empty-expression filter.
